## JustGo_mobile: minutes where avg view duration exceeded 30 s
One row for **every 1-minute window in the selected timeframe** (default: last 7 days) where the average view duration (`avg_ms`) of an OS went over **30 s (30,000 ms)**. Columns: `Time start` (start of the minute), `avg_ms`, `OS`. Widen the timeframe picker to look further back; an empty table means no minute breached.

- `duration` is converted to ms automatically (duration type in ns ÷ 1,000,000; a plain number is taken as ms).
- To change the threshold, edit `filter avg_ms > 30000`.

sections.title: JustGo_mobile minutes with avg view duration > 30 s

input.value:
fetch user.events
| filter characteristics.has_view_summary == true
| filter frontend.name == "JustGo_mobile"
// duration is a duration type (ns) in RUM -> ms; a plain number is taken as ms already
| fieldsAdd dur_ms = if(type(duration) == "duration", toDouble(duration) / 1000000, else: toDouble(duration))
| summarize avg_ms = avg(dur_ms), by: { time_start = bin(timestamp, 1m), os.name }
| filter avg_ms > 30000
| fields `Time start` = time_start, avg_ms = round(avg_ms, decimals: 0), OS = os.name
| sort `Time start` desc

The tile below runs **the same query on generated data**, so you can see the table with breaches. It makes up JustGo_mobile view events for Android, iOS and iPadOS over the last hour (3 per minute). Android goes over 30 s for two minutes and iOS for one; iPadOS never does. Times move with the current time. Nothing here reads real data.
